subject: MSA & Order Form: proposed SLA adjustments and ops/legal handoff
messages:
From: Megan Lee <megan.lee@aerofleet.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procure+contracts@aerofleet.com
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2025 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed SLA amendments for Order Form (MSA redlines attached)

Hannah / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — the team is happy with latency and throughput. Procurement has one set of asks before we can route to legal: primarily uptime guarantees and a clearer definition of planned maintenance. Attached is a redlined MSA with our requested SLA table (see tab "SLA_requests" in the OrderForm matrix). High level:

- 99.95% monthly uptime target for production endpoints (we're asking for a 15-minute rolling threshold for incident eligibility).
- Service credit ladder that scales to 20% of monthly fees for multi-hour incidents.
- Response times: P1 1 hour, P2 4 hours, P3 next business day.
- Require 14-day notice for non-emergency maintenance; emergency maintenance limited to security-critical patches and must be logged.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these, or where you'll need counters? We need a consolidated redline back by EOD Monday so internal sign-off can proceed.

Attachments: Aerofleet_MSA_redlines_20251218.pdf; OrderForm_SLA_matrix_v2.xlsx

Best,
Megan Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager
Aerofleet
From: hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com
To: Megan Lee <megan.lee@aerofleet.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 18 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA amendments for Order Form (MSA redlines attached)

Megan — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. We appreciate the fast timeline. Quick read-through and next steps below:

- We can accept the 99.95% target for the hosted production endpoints but need to align on the measurement window and what constitutes "endpoint availability" (per-route vs. per-account aggregation).
- The credit ladder is reasonable in principle, but engineering/finance need to validate the upper-bound percent on long-duration outages; suggest we propose a cap tied to actual service fees over the impacted region rather than a flat 20% in all cases.
- Response SLAs (P1/P2/P3) look doable operationally; we'll propose a slight wording tweak so "P1" is defined as "Complete service outage affecting >50% of traffic" to avoid noisy credits.
- Maintenance notice: 14 days for planned maintenance is acceptable; emergency maintenance carveouts okay provided we define examples and require post-facto incident reports and a timeline for mitigations.

I'm looping in Marissa (legal) and Jonas (ops) to draft a consolidated counter-redline. We'll aim to return a revised MSA and an updated OrderForm matrix by Monday EOD PST.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com, Megan Lee <megan.lee@aerofleet.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2025 08:27:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA amendments for Order Form (MSA redlines attached)

Megan / Hannah,

Marking up the redline now — a few legal notes up front:

1) Measurement and credits: request to define the metric as "aggregate regional availability for account-controlled production model endpoints" and exclude customer-side networking issues. We'll propose language for exclusion and measurement (synthetic checks + customer telemetry where available).

2) Cap on credits: propose a time-proportionate cap (e.g., credits calculated as % of monthly service fee capped at 50% of monthly fees per incident and 100% in aggregate for the month) — this balances Aerofleet's ask and our risk.

3) P1 definition: agree with Hanna's suggestion; will craft a P1/P2/P3 taxonomy with examples.

4) Maintenance: propose a two-tier approach — Routine maintenance (>=14 days notice) and Critical maintenance (<=72 hours notice with justification). All critical maintenance must include post-action report within 5 business days.

I'm attaching a legal-first redline. Note that I'm not finalizing the numeric caps without Ops input on how long we can reasonably tolerate the exposure. Jonas, can you validate the cap/credit math and whether we should tie the credit to region vs. account?

Attachment: Aerofleet_MSA_redlines_20251218_legal_comments.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com, Megan Lee <megan.lee@aerofleet.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2025 12:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA amendments for Order Form (MSA redlines attached)

Marissa / Hannah / Megan — operational feedback below after tabletop with SRE and finance: 

- Measurement: synthetic checks + internal telemetry will be our primary signal. We can make per-route windows available for customers but recommend basing credits on regional aggregated impact to avoid noisy slivers. Suggested wording: "Availability measured as percentage of successful inference requests across the region during the month, excluding customer network failures with evidence."

- Credit math: if Aerofleet insists on 20% as a single-incident cap, finance flags potential exposures on multi-region failovers. Ops recommends a tiered cap: 10% for incidents <4 hours, 25% for incidents 4-12 hours, and 50% for >12 hours — but with an overall monthly cap at 100% of monthly fees. If that's acceptable, we'll add monitoring and postmortem commitments.

- Response times: P1 = 1 hour response (ack + triage) with a 4-hour remediation SLA for simple fixes; complex remediation timelines will be in the incident report. This keeps the commercial ask but sets realistic repair windows.

- Maintenance: 14 days notice for routine; for critical security patches we will provide as much notice as possible and trigger the "critical maintenance" carveout. We'll commit to an incident report within 72 hours for critical patches (due to forensic analysis).

I'll patch the SLA matrix spreadsheet with the suggested credit ladder and monitoring notes. Hannah — once legal confirms wording we can send the consolidated redline back to Aerofleet and propose a 30-minute call Monday to close open items.

Jonas Weber
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Megan Lee <megan.lee@aerofleet.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 19 Dec 2025 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA amendments for Order Form (MSA redlines attached)

Hannah / Marissa / Jonas — appreciate the thoroughness and quick turnaround. Aerofleet procurement/ legal are generally aligned with the proposed tiered cap and the measurement language (we'll need the exact exclusion examples in the redline). Two asks before we finalize:

1) Can Redwood provide sample monitoring output (one week's synthetic checks and a sample regional availability report) to demonstrate measurement approach?
2) Please include a clause that emergency maintenance events are documented in a shared ticket (we use Jira; link is fine) and that postmortems are shared with a 5-business-day SLA for operational incidents that meet P1 criteria.

If you can include both items in the Monday redline and propose a 30-minute call at 10:00 AM PST Monday for final alignment, we can move to signatures the same week. Attaching a procurement acceptance checklist for your legal ops team to run through.

Attachment: Aerofleet_procurement_checklist_20251219.pdf

Thanks,
Megan Lee
Sr. Procurement Manager
Aerofleet
